name: Advanced Trauma Life Support: Primary Survey and Thoracic Emergencies

reference.source: ATLS 10th ed / Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed
clinicalPearls: Primary survey priority ABCDE: Airway with C-spine stabilization, Breathing, Circulation with hemorrhage control, Disability, Exposure
Tension pneumothorax: clinical diagnosis (hypotension, absent breath sounds, tracheal deviation); treat with immediate decompression, never delay for CXR
Cardiac tamponade: Beck triad (hypotension, jugular venous distension, muffled heart sounds); E-FAST demonstrates pericardial fluid
E-FAST assesses 6 acoustic windows: Morison pouch, splenorenal recess, suprapubic pouch, subxiphoid pericardium, bilateral pleural sliding
In hemodynamically unstable blunt trauma, a positive abdominal FAST mandates immediate exploratory laparotomy
reference.pathophysiology: Tension pneumothorax creates a one-way valve air leak into the pleural space. Positive intrathoracic pressure collapses the lung and shifts the mediastinum contralaterally, compressing the inferior and superior vena cavae and eliminating venous return, leading to electromechanical dissociation and death unless decompressed.
additionalDifferentials: Massive hemothorax (>1500 mL blood or >200 mL/hr for 2-4 hours)
additionalInvestigations: Extended Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (E-FAST)
Portable supine chest radiograph and pelvic radiograph in resuscitation bay
Contrast-enhanced whole-body CT (pan-scan) once hemodynamically stable
